title: བསྟན་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། དབུ་མ། ཤ (Derge Tengyur, vol. 106)
shelf_note: Derge woodblock folio of a Madhyamaka commentary on the applications of mindfulness and the two truths; belongs in the dbu ma section.

tr_errors_A.english: (absent; the quotation begins "If one does not see that which is to be felt...")
tr_errors_A.problem: First line of the Dharmasaṃgīti verse ('feeling is called experience') dropped; the rest of the verse is rendered correctly and the argument survives

tr_errors_A.english: that too is established other <note>than it</note>, namely by the intellect of another mental continuum
tr_errors_A.problem: གཞན་ཏེ ('by another, i.e.') garbled as 'other than it'; the following clause recovers the sense

tr_errors_A.english: Wishing simultaneously to teach the application of mindfulness to phenomena as the justification for that very point
tr_errors_A.problem: The two things taught together (the reasoning for that point, and mindfulness of phenomena) are collapsed into one

tr_errors_B.english: By what can the self experience anything?
tr_errors_B.problem: 'the self' is read into ཉིད; the verse asks what could experience anything, with no self introduced. Doctrinally loaded, but the verse's point (nothing experiences) still comes through

tr_errors_B.english: Apart from a deep-seated attachment to feelings, sensation
tr_errors_B.problem: 'to feelings' supplied; the object of the fixation is on the previous page

tr_errors_B.english: it does not exist as any kind of material thing
tr_errors_B.problem: dngos po (real entity) narrowed to 'material thing'

pages.prefer_reason: Neither has a serious error. A drops the opening line of the quoted verse and B reads 'the self' into the same verse. Each is one moderate slip in the same passage, and the rest of both is faithful, so neither is clearly better.

adjudication.claim: First verse line ཚོར་བ་ཉམས་མྱོང་ཞེས་བརྗོད་པ omitted (reviewer2: serious T8; reviewer1: moderate)
adjudication.why: The line is on the image (end of line 1 into the start of line 2) and A has no rendering of it. I rate it moderate, not serious: one definitional line is lost, the remaining five lines are correct, and the argument is unchanged.

adjudication.claim: Speaker reversal: 'Wishing to address an opponent's argument... he says if' gives the opponent's objection to the author
adjudication.why: B still says the untenability of the two truths is the opponent's argument and gives the 'if' clause as the objection. 'He says if' (the root-text author voicing the objection) is a normal way to read a commentary's lemma. No claim moves to the wrong speaker; at most a minor framing difference from གཞན་གྱིས...བརྩད་པར་འདོད་ནས.

adjudication.claim: 'By what can the self experience anything?' invents 'the self' (reviewer2: serious T1 with reversal; reviewer1: minor)
adjudication.why: Confirmed as a mistranslation of ཉིད, but rated moderate, not serious. It is not a reversal: the rhetorical question still says that nothing experiences.

adjudication.claim: OCR misreads: ན་ཉིད for གང་ཉིད, and མ་ཡིན་ཏེ for མེད་དེ
adjudication.why: At this resolution the print reads a single letter (ན) before ཉིད and reads པ་མ་ཡིན་ཏེ before དངོས་པོ, which matches the transcription. The canonical sūtra wording may differ, but the transcription follows this block.

book_verdict: A correct Derge Madhyamaka folio with a clean transcription. Both English versions are faithful in substance, and each has one moderate slip in the Dharmasaṃgīti verse.
